text: We should implement a dark theme for EXCAVA's interface. This choice enhances visual clarity and reduces eye strain, particularly in low-light environments. The trade-off is that it may require additional user education to navigate the changes initially, but the long-term benefits of a more enjoyable and engaging user experience outweigh this concern.

text: Pane: A dark theme hides real contrast issues in EXCAVA’s interface—users won’t notice unreadable text until they’re in bright sunlight. Instead, ship a toggle that defaults to system preference; that settles the argument by forcing us to fix visibility first, not aesthetics.

name: Pane
text: A live contrast checker adds complexity and may delay the rollout. Users might still overlook visibility problems if they prioritize aesthetics over functionality. A better approach is to conduct usability testing in varied lighting conditions first, revealing real accessibility issues before implementing any themes. This provides data to drive informed design choices rather than adding layers of potential confusion.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Conduct usability testing in varied lighting conditions to identify real accessibility issues before implementing any visual theme changes. The result must deliver a list of concrete, data-driven improvements to enhance visibility and usability, and Facet owns the testing and reporting of the results.
